Description: A theme-aware web component that brings the controls of a window, the pin and the minimize, maximize, restore and close controls, in one bar, and offers each of them to the host read-only. A host listens to a control, and works with it, through the taskbar.

template.description: The HTML template for the taskbar component.

div.bar.description: The surface that lays out its three zones, the start, the centre and the end, in a row or in a column.

div.start.description: The zone at the start of the bar. It holds the pin.

pin-button.description: The pin of the taskbar: the `pin-button` control, flat. The host defines `pin-button` and loads its template, before the taskbar. Cached as `elements.start.pin`: the taskbar offers it to the host as `pin` (see Controls).

div.center.description: The zone in the centre of the bar. It takes the room the start and the end leave, and holds the slot.

slot.description: The place where content the host places inside the taskbar, such as a title, is shown. The content is the host's own: the taskbar neither listens to it nor changes it.

div.end.description: The zone at the end of the bar. It holds the window controls, in this order.

minimize-button.description: The minimize control of the taskbar: the `minimize-button` control, flat. The host defines `minimize-button` and loads its template, before the taskbar. Cached as `elements.end.minimize`: the taskbar offers it to the host as `minimize` (see Controls).

maximize-button.description: The maximize control of the taskbar: the `maximize-button` control, flat. The host defines `maximize-button` and loads its template, before the taskbar. Cached as `elements.end.maximize`: the taskbar offers it to the host as `maximize` (see Controls).

restore-button.description: The restore control of the taskbar: the `restore-button` control, flat. The host defines `restore-button` and loads its template, before the taskbar. Cached as `elements.end.restore`: the taskbar offers it to the host as `restore` (see Controls).

close-button.description: The close control of the taskbar: the `close-button` control, flat. The host defines `close-button` and loads its template, before the taskbar. Cached as `elements.end.close`: the taskbar offers it to the host as `close` (see Controls).

visibility.description: Indicates whether the component is visible or hidden.

orientation.description: Indicates whether the controls are laid out side by side, in landscape, or one above the other, in portrait.

pin.description: The pin of the taskbar: the `pin-button` part itself, read-only, and `null` until the taskbar is connected. A host works with it through its own states, operations and events, as the specification of `pin-button` declares them, such as `taskbar.pin.pin()` and `taskbar.pin.hide()`. The taskbar dispatches no event of its own for it: a host listens on the control itself, such as `taskbar.pin.onpin`.

minimize.description: The minimize control of the taskbar: the `minimize-button` part itself, read-only, and `null` until the taskbar is connected. A host works with it through its own states, operations and events, as the specification of `minimize-button` declares them, such as `taskbar.minimize.minimize()` and `taskbar.minimize.hide()`. The taskbar dispatches no event of its own for it: a host listens on the control itself, such as `taskbar.minimize.onminimize`.

maximize.description: The maximize control of the taskbar: the `maximize-button` part itself, read-only, and `null` until the taskbar is connected. A host works with it through its own states, operations and events, as the specification of `maximize-button` declares them, such as `taskbar.maximize.maximize()` and `taskbar.maximize.hide()`. The taskbar dispatches no event of its own for it: a host listens on the control itself, such as `taskbar.maximize.onmaximize`.

restore.description: The restore control of the taskbar: the `restore-button` part itself, read-only, and `null` until the taskbar is connected. A host works with it through its own states, operations and events, as the specification of `restore-button` declares them, such as `taskbar.restore.restore()` and `taskbar.restore.hide()`. The taskbar dispatches no event of its own for it: a host listens on the control itself, such as `taskbar.restore.onrestore`.

close.description: The close control of the taskbar: the `close-button` part itself, read-only, and `null` until the taskbar is connected. A host works with it through its own states, operations and events, as the specification of `close-button` declares them, such as `taskbar.close.close()` and `taskbar.close.hide()`. The taskbar dispatches no event of its own for it: a host listens on the control itself, such as `taskbar.close.onclose`.

hide.description: Sets 'visibility' state to 'hidden' and hides the taskbar.

show.description: Sets 'visibility' state to 'visible' and shows the taskbar.

onhide.description: Dispatched when taskbar 'visibility' state changes from 'visible' to 'hidden'.

parameters.name: detail
parameters.description: Contains the new visibility state of the component.

onshow.description: Dispatched when taskbar 'visibility' state changes from 'hidden' to 'visible'.

parameters.name: detail
parameters.description: Contains the new visibility state of the component.
